findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class but is still registered as a concrete detector_handler
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class is still abstract. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at it, and `Detector.detector_handler` (models/detector.py) does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for any `Detector` row whose `type` is `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the handler was a working (no-op) concrete class, so this is a regression: `process_detectors` will now crash rather than skip for that detector type. Either implement the abstract methods (even as stubs raising NotImplementedError inside the method) or keep the previous concrete no-op handler until the real implementation lands. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector...` comment on line 10 is also now stale.

findings.title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with `group_key="group_key"` and `value=10`. `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` sets `fingerprint=handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, so the expected `IssueOccurrence` has fingerprint `["<id>:val1"]` while the handler will produce `["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality, so `expected_result` will not equal the actual result and the assertion on line 546-560 fails (or, if it somehow passes, it is not verifying the fingerprint at all). The expected occurrence should be built with `"group_key"` (and ideally the same value) so the test actually validates the occurrence the hook produces. Similarly, `test_state_results_multi_group` builds `occurrence_2` with value `6` while the packet has `group_2: 10`; it only passes because the mock ignores `value`.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still states "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Since the whole point of this change is to make the return keyed by group key to prevent duplicates, the docstring should describe the dict shape so implementers of other handlers are not misled.
